doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Segregation in the service
summary: Basic training in Texas had segregated units. A black pianist played with them but was kept in a separate area; nothing blatant was seen.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I wanted to just backtrack for a moment, in the service, you said that when you were with this band in ’43 you saw your first instance of segregation and so forth. What was the service like in that regard?

The same. We took Basic Training in Texas, and we mentioned something about that earlier, but there are some problems there, and the people were segregated pretty well. I think they had black units and all. There was a black piano player that — we didn’t have a piano player actually, I forget how that worked out — no I know what it was, the piano player that was with this group really wasn’t a jazz player. And we wanted to play sometimes. So there was this black piano player but we’d play with him. But he was in a different area from us, entirely. You know I didn’t see anything blatant at that time.
